description: UNSW Sydney publishes Python scripts used to visualise and assess the Urban-PLUMBER urban forcing dataset. The archive contains site-location mapping, comparisons of forcing series and bias-correction methods, plus a script collecting ERA5 mean values for urban locations. Some figure inputs and generated examples are included, while global settlement points and reanalysis data are external dependencies. The documented application uses 20 urban flux sites, with an ERA5 climatological comparison for 2000–2009. Zenodo provides a public ZIP under CC-BY-4.0, free with attribution, and identifies Python 3.8 with numerical and mapping libraries. This is diagnostic and plotting code, not a complete urban-climate simulator. Its input dependencies and publication-specific paths limit immediate portability. Modellers could adapt the correction comparisons when checking meteorological forcing before urban heat simulations. It complements the main processing pipeline with reproducible diagnostic routines. The environment and numerical results were not tested.
